problem_statement: Current AI Scientist prototypes often combine heterogeneous models into one narrative without proving that each model is used in its intended empirical setting. For this project, GAS-3 must support U.S. election simulation, IntervenSim must support intervention-aware social simulation, and STAP must support micro-video popularity prediction. Without an enforced routing and evidence contract, datasets, outputs and metrics can be silently mixed, making the resulting hypothesis difficult to falsify or reproduce.

rationale.innovation: Build a domain-aligned three-track AI Scientist: GAS-3 retains its hierarchical Group Agents inside a U.S.-election adapter; IntervenSim retains its source-crowd feedback loop for social events; STAP retains temporal enlargement and topology-aware memory for popularity curves. Qwen through Alibaba Cloud Bailian coordinates evidence, hypothesis drafting and review, but does not replace or cross-wire the three core engines.
reasoning_chain: GAS-3 represents behaviorally similar populations with hierarchical Group Agents, so state and voter-cohort agents can be evaluated as a population-weighted U.S.-election simulation rather than as individual voters.
IntervenSim explicitly feeds source interventions into crowd updates and aggregated responses back into the next intervention, which matches multi-round social-event simulation.
STAP was designed for micro-video popularity prediction and combines long-sequence temporal enlargement with a topology-aware historical-video memory bank.
Because the three engines solve different prediction objects, each requires its own Source/Target data, baselines, metrics and leakage controls even when they share one evidence and reporting layer.
An immutable application registry plus schema validation can prevent Qwen or configuration drift from remapping an engine, adding an unsupported fourth track or mixing evaluation claims.
If domain alignment is scientifically useful, each track should outperform its preregistered task-specific baseline on held-out data without relying on results from either of the other two tracks.
rationale.falsifiable_hypothesis: Under frozen chronological evaluation, the GAS-3 election adapter will improve calibrated state-level forecasting over historical carry-forward, IntervenSim will reduce social-trajectory error over a no-feedback baseline, and STAP will reduce popularity RMSE while improving rank correlation over flat retrieval. A track-level claim is rejected whenever its preregistered paired improvement is absent.

track_research_plans.problem_statement: Current U.S. election simulations often collapse heterogeneous voter cohorts into aggregate polling averages, weakening state-level uncertainty calibration and making the reasoning from cohort evidence to Electoral College outcomes difficult to audit.

rationale.innovation: Retain GAS-3 hierarchical Group Agents and population-weighted behavior quantization, then expose state-level aggregation, uncertainty and evidence lineage as a falsifiable election pipeline.
reasoning_chain: State outcomes depend on heterogeneous cohorts whose turnout and preference shifts are not represented by one national average.
GAS-3 can preserve cohort hierarchy and population weights while Qwen, called through Bailian, structures scenario evidence and agent rationales.
Aggregating frozen pre-election cohort states yields state scores and Electoral College distributions that can be backtested without leaking post-cutoff evidence.
Calibration and electoral-vote error can falsify whether hierarchical agents improve over polling and uniform-swing baselines.
rationale.falsifiable_hypothesis: Across held-out election cycles and preregistered pre-election cutoffs, GAS-3 will reduce state-level Brier score and electoral-vote MAE versus a uniform national swing baseline.

track_research_plans.paper_title: Auditable Hierarchical Group-Agent Simulation for State-Level U.S. Election Forecasting

paper_abstract.background: Aggregate election forecasts underrepresent cohort heterogeneity and hide the derivation of state-level uncertainty.
paper_abstract.methods: We propose a GAS-3 pipeline with hierarchical voter-cohort agents, population-weighted state aggregation, Qwen/Bailian evidence structuring and leakage-safe historical backtests.

track_research_plans.problem_statement: Existing social simulations frequently treat interventions as exogenous labels and do not close the source-intervention, crowd-response and public-signal feedback loop, limiting causal auditability and trajectory fidelity.

rationale.innovation: Execute IntervenSim as an endogenous multi-round feedback loop with explicit group state, interventions, public signals and reproducible artifacts.
reasoning_chain: Public reactions change after each source intervention and those reactions influence the next intervention.
A static rollout cannot represent this bidirectional dependence.
IntervenSim records source actions, group updates and population-weighted public signals on every round.
Held-out event trajectories can test whether the closed loop improves prediction and intervention-response accuracy over static rollouts.
rationale.falsifiable_hypothesis: On held-out events, the closed IntervenSim feedback loop will reduce normalized trajectory RMSE and intervention-response error versus a no-feedback simulation.

track_research_plans.paper_title: Closing the Intervention-Response Loop in Auditable Multi-Agent Social Simulation

paper_abstract.background: Social-event simulators rarely model how crowd response changes subsequent source intervention.
paper_abstract.methods: We implement an IntervenSim feedback loop with Qwen/Bailian source and crowd agents, population-weighted signals, explicit intervention traces and held-out trajectory evaluation.
paper_abstract.expected_results: We expect lower trajectory and intervention-response error than persistence and no-feedback baselines while retaining a complete execution audit.

methods.name: Group hierarchy
methods.procedure: Construct population groups and initial attitudes with no personally identifiable records.

methods.name: Feedback-loop execution
methods.procedure: Alternate source intervention, concurrent crowd updates and public-signal aggregation.

track_research_plans.problem_statement: Micro-video popularity models often sample too few frames and use flat historical retrieval, missing short salient intervals and topological relations among prior videos while offering limited evidence for their predictions.

rationale.innovation: Preserve STAP temporal enlargement and topology-aware parametric memory, then expose heat curves, frame importance and retrieved memory evidence as auditable outputs.
reasoning_chain: Sparse frame sampling can miss short visual events that influence popularity.
Dense sampling alone increases cost and does not organize relevant historical videos.
STAP jointly enlarges temporal evidence and addresses a topology-aware memory bank for multimodal prediction.
Prospective popularity labels and ablations can test whether both mechanisms improve error and ranking metrics over sequence and flat-memory baselines.
rationale.falsifiable_hypothesis: On licensed held-out micro-video data, STAP will reduce popularity RMSE and improve Spearman correlation versus LSTM and flat-retrieval baselines.

track_research_plans.paper_title: Auditable Spatio-Temporal Enlargement and Topology Memory for Micro-Video Popularity Prediction

paper_abstract.background: Sparse temporal evidence and flat historical memory limit micro-video popularity prediction.
paper_abstract.methods: We evaluate STAP temporal enlargement and topology-aware memory with multimodal inputs, Qwen/Bailian metadata reasoning, frame-level evidence and leakage-safe held-out videos.
paper_abstract.expected_results: We expect lower MAE/RMSE and higher rank correlation than MLP, LSTM and flat-memory baselines, with ablations identifying each component's contribution.

methods.name: Rights and split audit
methods.procedure: Validate dataset-specific rights and split videos by creator/time to avoid leakage.

methods.name: Temporal enlargement
methods.procedure: Combine sparse global frames with dense salient temporal neighborhoods.

methods.name: Topology-memory fusion
methods.procedure: Fuse visual, text and creator features with topology-aware historical memory.

methods.name: Evaluation and export
methods.procedure: Compute regression/ranking metrics and export frontend heat curves and frame evidence.

baselines.name: MLP fusion
baselines.description: Fuse pooled multimodal features without temporal modeling.

baselines.name: LSTM
baselines.description: Encode ordered frames without topology memory.

baselines.name: Flat retrieval
baselines.description: Retrieve historical features without topology-aware addressing.

metrics.name: Spearman rho
metrics.definition: Rank correlation between predicted and observed popularity.

experiments.split_strategy: Use official splits where licensed; otherwise group by creator and time so no creator/video crosses partitions.
experiments.decision_rule: Support only if STAP lowers RMSE and improves Spearman correlation versus the strongest preregistered baseline on held-out data.

paper_title: A Domain-Aligned Qwen AI Scientist for U.S. Election Simulation, Social Simulation, and Micro-Video Popularity Prediction

paper_abstract.background: AI Scientist systems can produce complete research narratives while still misaligning models, datasets and evaluation targets, weakening falsifiability across heterogeneous application modules.
paper_abstract.methods: We propose a three-track architecture that maps GAS-3 to U.S. election simulation, IntervenSim to intervention-aware social simulation and STAP to micro-video popularity prediction. Each track has separate Source/Target data and evaluation rules, while Qwen through Alibaba Cloud Bailian provides a shared schema-constrained evidence, hypothesis and review workflow.
paper_abstract.expected_results: We expect calibrated state forecasts, lower held-out social-trajectory error and more accurate popularity curves than task-specific baselines, with auditable datasets, real references and model-call provenance.

methods.name: Evidence intake and track routing
methods.procedure: Hash each source file, validate provenance and route evidence through the immutable three-track registry.

methods.name: GAS-3 U.S.-election adapter
methods.procedure: Create state and voter-cohort Group Agents, preserve population weights and quantify state win probabilities plus electoral-vote uncertainty.

methods.name: IntervenSim social simulation
methods.procedure: Run the unchanged source-intervention, crowd-update and public-signal feedback loop and persist every round artifact.

methods.name: STAP popularity prediction
methods.procedure: Apply sparse/dense temporal enlargement, multimodal fusion and topology-aware historical-video memory to predict the heat curve.

methods.name: Qwen research synthesis
methods.procedure: Call Qwen-Plus only through Bailian, allow only audited reference ids and validate all mandatory research-plan fields before review.

methods.name: Separate confirmatory evaluation
methods.procedure: Evaluate each track on its own frozen split, baselines and metrics; do not transfer a passing result from one track to another.
outputs: per-track metrics, intervals and rejection/retention decisions

baselines.name: Election historical carry-forward
baselines.description: Reuse the previous cycle's state winner or vote share.

baselines.name: Election regularized logistic
baselines.description: Predict state outcome from preregistered historical, polling and demographic features without Group Agents.

baselines.name: Social persistence
baselines.description: Use the previous engagement observation as the next social-simulation value.

baselines.name: IntervenSim no-feedback
baselines.description: Run group updates without feeding the aggregated public signal into the next source intervention.

baselines.name: Popularity MLP/LSTM
baselines.description: Use standard multimodal or sequential prediction without STAP topology-aware memory.

baselines.name: Popularity flat retrieval
baselines.description: Retrieve nearest historical videos without topology-aware clustering or temporal enlargement.

metrics.name: Election Brier score
metrics.definition: Mean squared error of state-level GAS-3 win probabilities against held-out outcomes.

metrics.name: Electoral-vote MAE
metrics.definition: Absolute error between predicted expected electoral votes and the held-out total.

metrics.name: Social normalized RMSE
metrics.definition: RMSE between normalized observed and IntervenSim engagement trajectories.

metrics.name: Social intervention-response error
metrics.definition: Absolute error in post-intervention change relative to the pre-intervention window.

metrics.name: Popularity RMSE
metrics.definition: RMSE of STAP-predicted micro-video popularity against the held-out target.

metrics.name: Popularity Spearman rho
metrics.definition: Rank correlation between predicted and observed micro-video popularity.

experiments.split_strategy: Election cycles are held out as complete units; social events use a chronological event-level split; popularity data use creator-disjoint chronological splits. No duplicate or derived record may cross partitions.
ablations: GAS-3: replace Group Agents with the regularized aggregate model
STAP: replace topology-aware memory with flat retrieval
shared layer: replace Qwen synthesis with deterministic schema templates
robustness_checks: election polling-cutoff and alternative population-weight sensitivity
social event-category leave-one-group-out and intervention-label noise
popularity creator/category leave-one-group-out and near-duplicate detection
bootstrap intervals across random seeds for every track
experiments.decision_rule: Retain a track-level claim only when its preregistered primary error decreases versus the named baseline and its paired 95% interval excludes zero after correction. Report partial support if one or two tracks pass; never claim all three from a result produced by only one track.

results.interpretation: All three tracks produced separate machine-readable feasibility evidence. Election and heat are bounded replay checks, while IntervenSim is the current actual execution; no cross-track result substitution occurred.
limitations: Election reconstruction is not a prospective forecast and may use target-derived historical priors.
The bundled social execution covers one event and does not establish external validity.
STAP evaluation replays supplied derived outputs rather than executing the full external checkpoint.
Confirmatory claims require preregistered target datasets, leakage-safe splits and human approval.

track_results.interpretation: The GAS-3 frontend/result contract executed across 50 states plus DC. Because the supplied display priors may derive from the same historical result, these metrics validate wiring and aggregation only.
track_results.claim_scope: Historical engineering reconstruction; no prospective predictive-validity claim.

track_results.interpretation: The current IntervenSim source-intervention, crowd-update and public-signal loop executed and emitted frontend-aligned trajectories. This establishes engineering feasibility for one event only.
track_results.claim_scope: Actual one-event simulation execution; no cross-event confirmatory claim.

track_results.interpretation: The supplied 78-row STAP-derived display output was replay-evaluated against its bundled labels. This verifies output parsing and metric computation, not fresh inference by the STAP checkpoint.
track_results.claim_scope: Derived display-artifact replay; full STAP checkpoint inference remains external.
